title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts Ledger Guide — Returned Repayments and New Plan Months
content:
Repayments on Benefit Overpayment Accounts that came back unpaid shorten a new repayment plan. The count is of the return entries booked on the overpayment within the 12 return-history months before the handling date; a return entry falls within them when the whole months from its booking date to the handling date are fewer than 12.

| Return entries on the overpayment within the 12 return-history months | Months taken off the plan months |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 12, the two-return reduction |
| Exactly one | 6, the one-return reduction |
| None | None |

## Reading the ledger

Return entries are the entries recording a repayment returned unpaid by the bank. Each return entry counts once.

*Hypothetical:* handling date 15 September. The overpayment's ledger shows return entries booked on 2 October of the previous year, 20 January and 3 June. The October entry is eleven whole months before 15 September and falls within the 12 months, as do the others: three returns, so 12 months are taken off.

*Hypothetical:* the same ledger with the October entry booked instead on 10 September of the previous year: that entry is twelve whole months before the handling date and falls outside, leaving two returns and the same 12-month reduction.
